analyst_view.overall: A Breton derby between Lorient (10th, 15 points) and Rennes (8th, 16 points), only one point apart after ten games. Lorient (Alexandre Dujeux) have one of the league's tightest defences, have beaten Rennes in their recent meetings including 2-0 at Roazhon Park in January, and won 2-0 at Le Havre before the break; Katseris is out and Isaak Touré (adductor) has now been ruled out, while Ibrahima Baldé is still a doubt, and the numbers already count all three as missing. Rennes have lost three of their last four (1-2 at home to Lille, 5-2 at Nice) and slid from first to eighth, with Franck Haise answering criticism from chairman Nicolas de Tavernost; top scorer Estéban Lepaul is back from his ankle sprain and in the squad, Frankowski is out (counted) and Rongier missed Friday's training but Haise says he is available. The numbers do not treat this as a derby, and referee Marc Bollengier (4.1 cards a game) is already in them.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.7 goals, with Lorient's tight defence and the absences of Touré, Katseris and Baldé already taken off Lorient's side. Lepaul, Rennes' top scorer, is back after missing the recent games the numbers learned from, so I lean slightly higher, to about 2.8; Touré being confirmed out matches what the numbers assumed, so it changes nothing.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.4 corners. Lorient's 3-4-2-1 and Rennes' 3-5-2 both lean on wing-backs, which the numbers already reflect, and Rennes having to break down a compact Lorient block is how this fixture usually plays out, so I stay at 9.4.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.3 cards with Bollengier's record (4.1 a game) already in, but they do not flag this as a derby. Breton derbies tend to be fierce and Rennes arrive under pressure from their chairman after a poor run, so I add a little, to about 4.6.

shots.text: The numbers say 25.9 shots, already allowing for Lorient's quieter attack lately and Rennes' busier one. Lepaul's return helps Rennes' finishing more than their volume of shots, and Lorient's compact style is unchanged, so I stay at 25.9.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.0 shots on target. A sharp striker like Lepaul back in the squad should put a few more efforts on target, but after a month out he may start on the bench behind Dia, so I nudge it up only to about 9.2.
